stem: Two engineers at Tidewater Bank each start a normal run in the same HCP Terraform workspace a minute apart, and the first run is still working. What happens to the second run?

choices.text: It fails immediately with an error saying the state is locked by the first run
It cancels the first run and takes its place in the workspace
It plans alongside the first run, and only its apply step waits
It stays pending in the workspace's queue until the first run finishes

rationale: Each workspace in HCP Terraform maintains its own queue of runs and processes them in order, so a run waiting for another to finish sits in a pending state. Failing immediately with a lock error is how Terraform itself behaves when it cannot take the state lock, which 6b covered; HCP Terraform queues the run instead. Nothing in the queue cancels an earlier run to replace it. The only runs that skip the queue are plan-only runs, which can proceed at any time and do not block other runs; a normal run waits as a whole rather than planning alongside the first.
